desc:
Slide a window of length k across nums from left to right. For every position, count how many different values are inside the window. Return these counts as an array of length nums.length - k + 1.

nums = [1, 2, 1, 3, 4, 2, 3], k = 4
windows: [1,2,1,3] [2,1,3,4] [1,3,4,2] [3,4,2,3]
result = [3, 4, 4, 3]
hints: Building a set for every window costs O(n * k).
Maintain a frequency map for the current window. A value is 'inside' as long as its frequency is above zero.
When sliding, increase the frequency of the new element (a new distinct value if it was 0 before) and decrease that of the leaving element (one fewer distinct value if it drops to 0).
editorial: Keep a hash map from value to its count in the window and a variable distinct for the number of keys with a positive count. Adding an element whose count goes from 0 to 1 increases distinct; removing an element whose count goes from 1 to 0 decreases it.
Record distinct after the first k elements and after every slide. Each step does O(1) expected work, so the total is O(n) time with O(k) extra space for the map.
